Scaling IDE models

1 Simulation

We create a simple model with downward-movement and diffusion, on 400 cosine basis functions.

import jax
# Some filters, particularily the sqrt filters, may work in 32-bit, but expect instabilities.
jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
import jax.numpy as jnp

# Module imports
import jaxidem.utils as utils
import jaxidem.idem as idem

seed = 4
key = jax.random.PRNGKey(seed)
keys = jax.random.split(key, 10)


T = 20
nobs = 100
process_basis = utils.place_cosine_basis(N=10) 

# This puts a point of mass at 0.1,0.9 and a point of 0 at 0.9, 0.1.
# Using the least squares estimator, this creates a point at the corner.
inp_data = jnp.array([[0.1, 0.9, 100],
#                      [0.9, 0.1, 0],
                      [0.3, 0.9, 100],
                      [0.1, 0.7, 100],
                      [0.3, 0.7, 100]])


# create a 'ball' at the top left using least squares
PHI = process_basis.mfun(inp_data[:,0:2])
alpha_0 = jnp.linalg.pinv(PHI.T@PHI)@PHI.T @ inp_data[:,2]



# this function creates models like in this example. for practical uses, use `init_model`.

# Fudged numbers to look at least a little interesting.
K_basis = (
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
)
# These values create reasonable drift and diffusion at
s = 0.0001
k = (
    jnp.array([1/(2*jnp.pi*s)]), # Scale parameter    (θ_1)
    jnp.array([0.5*s]), # Shape paramter  (θ_2)
    jnp.array([-0.025]), # X-axis drift    (θ_3) 
    jnp.array([0.025]), # Y-axis drift     (θ_4)
)
kernel = idem.param_exp_kernel(K_basis, k)

model = idem.gen_example_idem(keys[0],
                              process_basis = process_basis,
                              beta = jnp.array([0.0]),
                              kernel=kernel)




coords = jax.random.uniform(
                keys[0],
                shape=(nobs, 2),
                minval=0,
                maxval=1,
            )
times = jnp.repeat(jnp.arange(1, T + 1), coords.shape[0])
rep_coords = jnp.tile(coords, (T, 1))
x = rep_coords[:,0]
y = rep_coords[:,1]


process_data, obs_data = model.simulate(keys[1], x, y, times, alpha_0 = alpha_0)

# For normalising axes
zmin = float(jnp.nanmin(obs_data.z))
zmax = float(jnp.nanmax(obs_data.z))
zbounds = [zmin, zmax]
frames, traces = plotly_st_scatter(process_data, title="Observations", mark_size=20, zbounds=zbounds)
process_fig = make_interactive_fig(traces)

# Apply the catppuccin mocha theme to match these notebooks
plotters.apply_catppuccin_mocha(process_fig, fontsize = 20)

process_fig.update_layout(
    xaxis=dict(showticklabels=False),
    yaxis=dict(showticklabels=False, scaleanchor="x")
)
 
process_fig.show()
frames, traces = plotly_st_scatter(obs_data, title="Observations", mark_size=20, zbounds=zbounds)
obs_fig = make_interactive_fig(traces)

# Apply the catppuccin mocha theme to match these notebooks
plotters.apply_catppuccin_mocha(obs_fig, fontsize = 20)

obs_fig.update_layout(
    xaxis=dict(showticklabels=False),
    yaxis=dict(showticklabels=False, scaleanchor="x")
)

obs_fig.show()

Once we simulate the data, we can ‘filter’ across it, recovering the means and variances of the process. This is built-in the the method idem.Model.filter

# Some filters dont work yet!
filt_data, filt_results = model.filter(
    obs_data,
    method="kalman",
#    P_0 = 10*jnp.eye(model.nbasis)
)

frames, traces = plotly_st_scatter(filt_data, title="Observations", mark_size=20, zbounds=zbounds)
filt_fig = make_interactive_fig(traces)

# Apply the catppuccin mocha theme to match these notebooks

    method="kalman",
)

frames, traces = plotly_st_scatter(smooth_data, title="Observations", mark_size=20, zbounds=zbounds)
smooth_fig = make_interactive_fig(traces)

# Apply the catppuccin mocha theme to match these notebooks
plotters.apply_catppuccin_mocha(smooth_fig, fontsize = 20)

smooth_fig.update_layout(
    xaxis=dict(showticklabels=False),
    yaxis=dict(showticklabels=False, scaleanchor="x")
)

smooth_fig.show()
log_marginal_kal = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="kalman", likelihood='full')
log_marginal_skal = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="skalman", likelihood='full')
log_marginal_ikal = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="ikalman", likelihood='full')
log_marginal_sikal = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="sikalman", likelihood='full')
log_marginal_sqrt = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="sqrt", likelihood='full')
log_marginal_inf = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="inf", likelihood='full')
log_marginal_sqinf = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="sqinf", likelihood='full')
log_marginal_pkal = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="parallel", likelihood='full')
#log_marginal_psqrt = model.get_log_like(obs_data, method="psqrt", likelihood='full')

nreps = 1

time_kal   = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_kal, model.params, n=nreps)
time_skal  = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_skal, model.params, n=nreps)
time_ikal  = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_ikal, model.params, n=nreps)
time_sikal  = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_sikal, model.params, n=nreps)
time_inf   = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_inf, model.params, n=nreps)
time_sqrt  = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_sqrt, model.params, n=nreps)
time_sqinf = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_sqinf, model.params, n=nreps)
time_pkal  = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_pkal, model.params, n=nreps)
#time_psqrt = utils.time_jit(key, log_marginal_psqrt, model.params, n=nreps)

data = [
    ["kal",   time_kal.compile_time,   time_kal.average_time * 1000,   time_kal.value],
    ["skal",  time_skal.compile_time,  time_skal.average_time * 1000,  time_skal.value],
    ["ikal",  time_ikal.compile_time,  time_ikal.average_time * 1000,  time_ikal.value],
    ["sikal",  time_sikal.compile_time,  time_sikal.average_time * 1000,  time_sikal.value],
    ["inf",   time_inf.compile_time,   time_inf.average_time * 1000,   time_inf.value],
    ["sqrt",  time_sqrt.compile_time,  time_sqrt.average_time * 1000,  time_sqrt.value],
    ["sqinf", time_sqinf.compile_time, time_sqinf.average_time * 1000, time_sqinf.value],
    ["pkal",  time_pkal.compile_time,  time_pkal.average_time * 1000,  time_pkal.value],
#    ["psqrt", time_psqrt.compile_time, time_psqrt.average_time * 1000, time_psqrt.value],
]

import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=["Method", "Compile Time (s)", "Average Time (ms)", "Log Likelihood"])
print(f"Results for IDEM with nbasis={model.nbasis}, nobs = {nobs}, T = {T}")
print(f"Precision: {model.M.dtype}")

print(df.to_markdown(index=False))

2 Fitting

# Fudged numbers to look at least a little interesting.
K_basis = (
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
    utils.place_basis(nres=1, min_knot_num=1, basis_fun=lambda s, r: 1),
)
# These values create reasonable drift and diffusion at
s = 0.0005
k = (
    jnp.array([1/(2*jnp.pi*s)]), # Scale parameter    (θ_1)
    jnp.array([2*s]), # Shape paramter  (θ_2)
    jnp.array([0.]), # X-axis drift    (θ_3) 
    jnp.array([0.]), # Y-axis drift     (θ_4)
)
kernel = idem.param_exp_kernel(K_basis, k)

shell_model = idem.gen_example_idem(keys[0],
                                    process_basis = process_basis,
                                    beta = jnp.array([0.0]),
                                    kernel=kernel)

bound_di = jnp.max(shell_model.process_grid.ngrids * shell_model.process_grid.deltas)


print(f"\nTrue Parameters:\n{idem.format_params(model.params)}\n")    

print(f"\nInitial Parameters:\n{idem.format_params(shell_model.params)}\n")

nll_val_grad = jax.value_and_grad(
    shell_model.get_log_like(
        obs_data, method='sqrt', likelihood="partial", negative=True
    )
)

import optax

optimizer=optax.adam(1e-2)

nll, _ = nll_val_grad(shell_model.params)
params = shell_model.params
opt_state = optimizer.init(params)


print(
    f"""The log likelihood (up to a constant) of the initial model is
    {-nll}"""
)

for i in range(10):
    nllprev = nll
    nll, grad = nll_val_grad(params)
    updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(grad, opt_state, params=params)
    params = optax.apply_updates(params, updates)


print(
    f"""The final log likelihood (up to a constant) of the fit model is
    {-nll}"""
)

new_fitted_model = shell_model.update(params)

print(f"\nFinal Parameters:\n{idem.format_params(new_fitted_model.params)}\n")
